q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT T.CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) CPC FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID ) T JOIN (SELECT COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) PC FROM PRODUCT) T2 WHERE PC = CPC

counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 1), (4, 2), (4, 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks if there is at least one customer who has purchased all distinct products, while Q2 checks if all customers have purchased the same number of distinct products as the total number of distinct products.
counterexample_dsp: A scenario where Q1 returns true but Q2 returns false is when there are multiple customers, each purchasing a unique product, and an additional customer purchasing all products.
